── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 40, 42, 46, 34 mi
This week: 41 mi over 5 runs.
Raced: Sun Oct 18, 26.22 mi in 3h 50m
Pain noted: Sun 3/10 (Quads and calves very sore, normal marathon sore I think)
Body: "Quads are wrecked, stairs are hard. Blister on my left big toe."
Feeling: "Proud and tired."
Asks: "How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks."

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Big result on Sunday, 3:50 and a 12-minute PR on a hilly course. …
Answers: (1) Give the legs a full week off running first. Walk when you feel like moving, and let the blister close. (2) The Thanksgiving 10K in 5 weeks is doable, but only as a steady run, not a race. Hard 10K efforts in week 3 or 4 after a marathon are where people pick up niggles, and you have nothing to prove five weeks after a PR.
Safety flag: Normal soreness vs something more
Next week:
Mon: rest, walking only if you feel like moving, nothing structured. Day one after 26.2…
Tue: rest, optional 20 to 30 min easy walk. Keeps blood moving without loading the quads.
Wed: rest, optional 20 to 30 min easy walk. Still letting the deep soreness clear.
Thu: easy, 2 mi, very easy and only if stairs feel normal and the blister has closed…
Fri: rest, walk if you want. Protect whatever Thursday showed us.
Sat: easy, 3 mi, conversational, flat route, heart rate under 140. Short shakeout to see…
Sun: easy, 3 to 4 mi, conversational, stop if anything pinches. Gentle close to week…
